$what: HOW MUCH EVIDENCE EACH AGENT SEES, named so it can be changed.
$why: These were literals at their call sites — head -c 8000 of a gate log, head -40 of a compiler's
output, head -100 of a source file — and every one decides what an agent is shown and therefore
what it can conclude. A number with no name cannot be tuned by an operator, cannot appear in a
cost estimate, and cannot be found by anyone asking why an agent missed something that was three
Declared here so a project can widen a window when its evidence is larger, and so the audit that
counts unnamed decisions stops counting these.
UNITS ARE IN THE NAME. `Chars` is a byte window (head -c); `Lines` is a line window (head -n).

gateLogChars.$why: A QA gate's log, handed to the self-heal analyst. Long enough for a stack trace and the assertion around it.

lintLogChars.$why: The lint log for the same analyst — same shape of evidence, same window.

typecheckLines.$why: Compiler errors are one line each and the first are the causes; the rest are usually consequences.

lintFindingLines.$why: Lint findings handed to a writer as a correction list.

failureExcerptLines.$why: A failing test's output. Wide, because the assertion and the value that produced it can be far apart.

mutationSourceLines.$why: The source file a mutant-hunter reasons about.

mutationTestLines.$why: The test file paired with it.

storyTitleLines.$why: A list of story titles for context, not for analysis.

testOutputLines.$why: A failing or timed-out test run, appended to what the writer reads. The assertion and the values that produced it are usually near the top.

typecheckErrorLines.$why: New type errors introduced by a story, handed to the writer as the thing to fix.

lintOutputLines.$why: Lint violations in files this story changed — the writer must fix these or the pre-commit hook reverts its work.

changedFileLines.$why: The list of files a story changed, shown as context rather than analysed.

tamperedFileLines.$why: Files touched inside a vendored directory. A handful names the problem; a long list does not change the verdict.

declaredDependenciesInPrompt.$why: The project's declared dependencies, given to the mint. On 2026-08-07 an empty estate made it invent a vendor, so this list is the guard against that — wide, because the cost of missing one is a whole roster briefed on the wrong product.

quotesPerDocument.$why: Quotes carried from each ticket-linked document. Enough to establish what the source says without pasting the document.

fixSitesInPrompt.$why: Located fix sites shown to the spec agent so it anchors criteria to real code rather than guessing.

filesPerStory.$why: A story's own declared files. A handful is a story; more is a story that should have been split.

vcSubjectChars.$why: The subject line of a fallback verification criterion, trimmed so a whole description does not become the criterion.

fixSitesForReproWriter.$why: Fix sites shown to the repro-test writer, so the test it writes exercises the located behaviour rather than a guess.

vcsForReproWriter.$why: Verification criteria shown alongside them — the observable behaviour the test must assert.

reproFailureJsonChars.$why: The failure payload returned when a written test fails against the committed fix, fed back so the writer can correct it.

quarantineRawChars.$why: The raw agent output kept on a quarantined KB record. Enough to diagnose why it was rejected without storing an entire transcript.

qaGateDiffLines.$why: The phase diff handed to a QA gate. Was an undeclared head -2000 at the runtime-boundary call site, beside a diff base (${_rev_base:-HEAD~1}) that nothing ever set.

$whyCeilingsRaised: RAISED VERY HIGH 2026-09-23, deliberately. Every one of these was a wall that stopped work or hid the evidence an agent needed, and each was found one at a time by a paid run: the analyst's remedy truncated to 200 characters, the writer shown 60 lines of a failing suite, three files of a story, 400 lines of the file it was rewriting. Until a programme runs clean end to end, NO ceiling here may be the reason anything stops or anything is unseen. These are not tuned values; they are deliberately far above any observed need, and they get tuned down only with evidence from a green run.
